source.text: הָיְתָ֣ה עָלַי֮ יַד־יְהוָה֒ וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נִי בְר֨וּחַ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְנִיחֵ֖נִי בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבִּקְעָ֑ה וְהִ֖יא מְלֵאָ֥ה עֲצָמֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: There was on me [the] hand of Yahweh, and he brought me out by [the] Spirit of Yahweh and set me down in the middle of the valley, and it [was] full of bones.

en.L: The hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was upon me, and by the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me out and set me down in the valley's midst; and it [was] full of bones.
en.B: The hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} carried me out by the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and put me down in the middle of the valley. It was full of bones.
en.R: The power of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me. By {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} took me out and put me down in the middle of a valley. The valley was full of bones.

pt.L: A mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava sobre mim, e pelo Espírito {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me levou para fora e me pôs no meio do vale; e ele [estava] cheio de ossos.
pt.B: A mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio sobre mim, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me levou para fora pelo Espírito {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} e me deixou no meio do vale. O vale estava cheio de ossos.
pt.R: O poder {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio sobre mim. Pelo {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Espírito, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me levou para fora e me deixou no meio de um vale. O vale estava cheio de ossos.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon me: the LORD's power took hold of me
decisions.reason: See 1:3. The phrase opens a new vision, as in 8:1 and 40:1.

decisions.choice: by the Spirit of the LORD: the LORD's Spirit carries Ezekiel
decisions.reason: As in 3:12-14; 8:3 and 11:1, 24, the Spirit lifts and carries Ezekiel in the vision (see 2:2). The word *ruach* will be used ten times in this passage, in its three senses: Spirit, breath and wind (see verse 5).

decisions.choice: the valley full of bones: a battlefield of the unburied dead
decisions.reason: The article ("the valley") may point to the plain where Ezekiel saw the glory in 3:22-23. The bones lie scattered and unburied, like those of an army killed in battle (verse 9, "these slain"). To be left unburied was a curse (Deuteronomy 28:26; Jeremiah 8:1-2).

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon me (L); came on me (B); the power of the LORD came on me (R); Spirit, capitalized
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula and for *ruach* where the Spirit lifts or carries Ezekiel (2:2). Readable names the LORD as the subject for clarity. The vision is narrative, so its dialogue takes double quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

decisions.choice: o Espírito do SENHOR (every level)
decisions.reason: Where ruach lifts and carries Ezekiel it is the LORD's own Spirit (m2), so "Espírito" takes a capital, as in the English; the formula "a mão do SENHOR" follows 1:3.

source.text: וְהֶעֱבִירַ֥נִי עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם סָבִ֣יב׀סָבִ֑יב וְהִנֵּ֨ה רַבּ֤וֹת מְאֹד֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַבִּקְעָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה יְבֵשׁ֥וֹת מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made me pass by them all around, all around; and look, very many [were] on the face of the valley, and look, very dry.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led me around among them, all around; and look, [there were] very many on the surface of the valley, and look, [they were] very dry.
en.B: He led me back and forth among them, and I saw that there were a great many of them on the floor of the valley, and they were very dry.
en.R: He led me all around among the bones. There were a great many of them on the ground in the valley, and they were very dry.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me fez passar por entre eles, ao redor, por toda a volta; e eis que [havia] muitíssimos sobre a superfície do vale, e eis que [estavam] muito secos.
pt.B: Ele me fez andar de um lado para o outro entre eles, e vi que eram muitíssimos, espalhados pelo chão do vale, e estavam muito secos.
pt.R: Ele me levou por todo o vale, no meio dos ossos. Havia uma quantidade enorme de ossos no chão do vale, e eles estavam muito secos.

decisions.choice: very many and very dry: long dead, beyond all hope
decisions.reason: The bones have lain there a long time. Nothing in them suggests that life could return (verse 11). The word "very" is repeated to stress it.

decisions.choice: led me back and forth (B); all around (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "all around". Literal keeps "all around"; Balanced and Readable give its sense. Literal keeps "look" twice for the Hebrew *hinneh*, which marks what Ezekiel saw; Balanced says "I saw".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הֲתִחְיֶ֖ינָה הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֕ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אַתָּ֥ה יָדָֽעְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, will these bones live? And I said, Lord Yahweh, you know.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I said, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know."
en.B: He asked me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" I answered, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know."
en.R: He asked me, "Son of man, can these bones come back to life?" I answered, "Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know that."

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Filho do homem, estes ossos podem viver?" E eu disse: "Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sabes."
pt.B: Ele me perguntou: "Filho do homem, será que estes ossos podem viver?" Eu respondi: "Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, só {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sabes."
pt.R: Ele me perguntou: "Filho do homem, estes ossos podem voltar a viver?" Eu respondi: "Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, só {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sabes isso."

decisions.choice: Lord GOD, you know: the answer leaves it to the LORD
decisions.reason: Ezekiel neither says yes nor no. By human reckoning the answer is no; only the LORD knows what he can do. The Hebrew stresses "you": you yourself know.

decisions.choice: will these bones live: can they come to life again
decisions.reason: The verb "live" runs through the passage (verses 5, 6, 9, 10, 14). The question is whether the dead can live.

decisions.choice: only you know (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses "you" by adding the pronoun. Balanced and Readable say "only you" to carry the stress. "Lord GOD" is *Adonai YHWH*, as set for Ezekiel.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י הִנָּבֵ֖א עַל־הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם הָעֲצָמוֹת֙ הַיְבֵשׁ֔וֹת שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Prophesy over these bones and say to them, Dry bones, hear [the] word of Yahweh.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Prophesy over these bones, and say to them, Dry bones, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Prophesy over these bones and say to them, Dry bones, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Prophesy to these bones. Tell them, Dry bones, listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says!

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Profetiza sobre estes ossos e dize a eles: Ossos secos, ouçam a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Profetiza sobre estes ossos e dize a eles: Ossos secos, escutem a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}!
pt.R: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Profetiza para estes ossos. Dize a eles: Ossos secos, escutem o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz!

decisions.choice: prophesy over these bones: the word of the LORD addressed to the dead
decisions.reason: Ezekiel is told to preach to corpses. It is the LORD's word, not the prophet's power, that will bring life (compare Genesis 1:3; Psalm 33:6).

decisions.choice: no inner quotation marks for the message
decisions.reason: By the rule set for Ezekiel, the message the prophet is told to deliver takes no quotation marks of its own, as in 11:5; the LORD's words to Ezekiel take double quotation marks because the vision is narrative. The LORD's speech runs to the end of verse 6.

decisions.choice: Profetiza, dize (tu) to Ezekiel; ouçam, escutem (vocês) to the bones
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks to Ezekiel with "tu", as the Ezekiel notes set for the book, and the prophet speaks to the bones as a group with "vocês". Balanced and Readable say "escutem" rather than "ouçam", the plain word for listening to a message.

source.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לָעֲצָמ֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנִ֜י מֵבִ֥יא בָכֶ֛ם ר֖וּחַ וִחְיִיתֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh to these bones: Look, I am bringing into you breath, and you will live.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} to these bones: Look, I am going to make breath enter you, and you will live.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this to these bones: I am going to put breath into you, and you will come to life.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says to these bones: I am going to put breath into you, and you will come back to life.

pt.L: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} a estes ossos: Eis que farei entrar fôlego em vocês, e vocês viverão.
pt.B: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} a estes ossos: Vou pôr fôlego dentro de vocês, e vocês ganharão vida.
pt.R: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz a estes ossos: Vou pôr fôlego em vocês, e vocês vão voltar à vida.

decisions.choice: breath: *ruach*, one word for breath, wind and Spirit
decisions.reason: The Hebrew *ruach* means wind, breath and spirit, and verses 1-14 use all three senses of it. It is the Spirit of the LORD who carries Ezekiel (verse 1); breath that enters the bodies and makes them live (verses 5-6, 8-10); the four winds from which the breath is called (verse 9); and the LORD's own Spirit, which he will put in his people (verse 14). The passage plays on the one word: the breath that makes the bodies live comes from the winds and stands for the Spirit of God. The breath of life recalls Genesis 2:7, where God breathes into the man he has formed, and Psalm 104:29-30. Each verse states which sense it gives; the reader should know that behind all of them stands one Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: I will make breath enter you, and you will live: Genesis 2:7
decisions.reason: As God formed the man from dust and breathed into him the breath of life (Genesis 2:7), so here he first rebuilds the bodies (verses 6-8) and then gives them breath (verses 9-10). The restoration of Israel is pictured as a new creation.

decisions.choice: breath (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Here *ruach* is the breath of life that makes a body live, so every level says "breath" (m1). Readable says "come back to life" for "live", since the bones were dead. The formula follows 2:4.

decisions.choice: fôlego (every level)
decisions.reason: Ruach is used in verses 1-14 in three senses, and Portuguese, like English, needs three words (m1): "Espírito" where the LORD's Spirit is meant (verses 1, 14), "fôlego" for the breath that makes a body live (verses 5-10), "ventos" for the four winds (verse 9). "Fôlego" is the everyday word for the breath of life ("fôlego de vida", Genesis 2:7) and says plainly that the bodies are to breathe; "espírito" here would hide the picture.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּי֩ עֲלֵיכֶ֨ם גִּדִ֜ים וְֽהַעֲלֵתִ֧י עֲלֵיכֶ֣ם בָּשָׂ֗ר וְקָרַמְתִּ֤י עֲלֵיכֶם֙ ע֔וֹר וְנָתַתִּ֥י בָכֶ֛ם ר֖וּחַ וִחְיִיתֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will put on you sinews and bring up on you flesh and cover over you skin and put in you breath, and you will live; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: And I will put on you sinews, and I will bring up flesh on you, and I will overlay you with skin, and I will put in you breath, and you will live; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: I will put tendons on you and make flesh grow on you and cover you with skin. I will put breath in you, and you will come alive. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: I will put tendons on you. I will make muscles grow on you and cover you with skin. I will put breath in you, and you will come back to life. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

pt.L: E porei tendões sobre vocês, e farei crescer carne sobre vocês, e os cobrirei de pele, e porei fôlego em vocês, e vocês viverão; e vocês saberão que eu [sou] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}."
pt.B: Porei tendões em vocês, farei crescer carne sobre vocês e os cobrirei de pele. Porei fôlego em vocês, e vocês ganharão vida. Então vocês saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}."
pt.R: Vou colocar tendões em vocês. Vou fazer crescer músculos em vocês e vou cobri-los de pele. Vou pôr fôlego em vocês, e vocês vão voltar à vida. Então vocês saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}."

decisions.choice: sinews: the tendons and ligaments that hold the body together
decisions.reason: The word means the cords that bind muscle to bone (Job 10:11). The bodies are rebuilt in order: sinews, flesh, skin, and last of all breath.

decisions.choice: sinews, flesh, skin, breath: Job 10:11
decisions.reason: Job describes his own making in the same order: "You clothed me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and sinews" (Job 10:11).

decisions.choice: breath; the refrain as settled
decisions.reason: *Ruach* is "breath" here, as in verse 5. The refrain follows the settled wording. Readable says "muscles" for "flesh", since the word means the body's flesh. The closing quotation mark ends the LORD's words to Ezekiel begun in verse 4.

source.text: וְנִבֵּ֖אתִי כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צֻוֵּ֑יתִי וַֽיְהִי־ק֤וֹל כְּהִנָּֽבְאִי֙ וְהִנֵּה־רַ֔עַשׁ וַתִּקְרְב֣וּ עֲצָמ֔וֹת עֶ֖צֶם אֶל־עַצְמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I prophesied as I was commanded; and there was a sound as I prophesied, and look, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone.

en.L: And I prophesied just as I had been commanded; and there was a sound as I prophesied, and look, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to its bone.
en.B: So I prophesied as I had been told. While I was prophesying, there was a noise, a rattling sound, and the bones came together, each bone to its own bone.
en.R: So I did what I was told and prophesied. While I was speaking, I heard a noise, a loud rattling. The bones began to come together. Each bone joined the bone it belonged to.

pt.L: E profetizei conforme me havia sido ordenado; e houve um ruído enquanto eu profetizava, e eis um estalar, e os ossos se aproximaram, osso junto ao seu osso.
pt.B: Profetizei, então, como me havia sido mandado. Enquanto eu profetizava, houve um ruído, um estalar de ossos, e os ossos foram se juntando, cada um ao osso que lhe correspondia.
pt.R: Então fiz o que me mandaram e profetizei. Enquanto eu falava, ouvi um barulho, um estalar forte. Os ossos começaram a se juntar. Cada osso se encaixou no osso ao qual pertencia.

decisions.choice: a rattling: a shaking, a clattering noise
decisions.reason: The word *ra'ash* means shaking or quaking, and it is used of earthquakes (38:19; Amos 1:1). Here it is the clatter of the bones coming together.

decisions.choice: I prophesied as I was commanded: Ezekiel's obedience
decisions.reason: The prophet does exactly what he is told (12:7; 24:18), and the LORD's word does what it says (Isaiah 55:10-11).

decisions.choice: a rattling (L, B); a loud rattling (R)
decisions.reason: Each level says "rattling" for the sound, not "earthquake", since the bones are the subject.

decisions.choice: um estalar (L, B); um estalar forte (R)
decisions.reason: The word means shaking (m1); here it is the noise of the bones knocking together, and "estalar" is the sound of bones and wood striking, as the English "rattling". "Terremoto" would make the earth the subject.

source.text: וְרָאִ֜יתִי וְהִנֵּֽה־עֲלֵיהֶ֤ם גִּדִים֙ וּבָשָׂ֣ר עָלָ֔ה וַיִּקְרַ֧ם עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם ע֖וֹר מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְר֖וּחַ אֵ֥ין בָּהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I looked, and look, on them sinews, and flesh came up, and skin covered over them above; but breath there was none in them.

en.L: And I looked, and look, there were sinews on them, and flesh had come up, and skin had covered them over; but there was no breath in them.
en.B: As I watched, tendons appeared on them, flesh grew on them, and skin covered them over. But there was no breath in them.
en.R: As I watched, tendons and muscles grew on the bones, and skin covered them. But they were not breathing.

pt.L: E olhei, e eis que [havia] tendões sobre eles, e a carne tinha subido, e a pele os havia coberto por cima; mas fôlego não havia neles.
pt.B: Enquanto eu olhava, apareceram tendões sobre eles, a carne cresceu e a pele os cobriu. Mas não havia fôlego neles.
pt.R: Enquanto eu olhava, tendões e músculos cresceram sobre os ossos, e a pele os cobriu. Mas eles não respiravam.

decisions.choice: there was no breath in them: bodies without life
decisions.reason: The bodies are whole, but they are still corpses. Rebuilding them is not enough; they need breath, the gift of life from God. The step echoes Genesis 2:7, where the man is formed before he receives the breath of life.

decisions.choice: breath (L, B); they were not breathing (R)
decisions.reason: *Ruach* is "breath" here, as in verses 5-6.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל־הָר֑וּחַ הִנָּבֵ֣א בֶן־אָ֠דָם וְאָמַרְתָּ֨אֶל־הָר֜וּחַ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה מֵאַרְבַּ֤ע רוּחוֹת֙ בֹּ֣אִי הָר֔וּחַ וּפְחִ֛י בַּהֲרוּגִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְיִֽחְיֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: From [the] four winds come, breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and you will say to the breath, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: From the four winds come, breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live."
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me, "Prophesy to the breath. Prophesy, son of man, and say to it, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Come from the four winds, breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live."
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, prophesy to the breath. Say to it, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Breath, come from the four winds! Breathe into these people who were killed, so that they may live again."

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Profetiza ao fôlego; profetiza, filho do homem, e dirás ao fôlego: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Dos quatro ventos vem, ó fôlego, e sopra sobre estes que foram mortos, para que vivam."
pt.B: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Profetiza ao fôlego. Profetiza, filho do homem, e dize a ele: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Vem dos quatro ventos, ó fôlego, e sopra dentro destes que foram mortos, para que vivam."
pt.R: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Filho do homem, profetiza ao fôlego. Dize a ele: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Fôlego, vem dos quatro ventos! Sopra dentro destas pessoas que foram mortas, para que vivam de novo."

decisions.choice: the breath ... the four winds: the same word in two senses
decisions.reason: Ezekiel speaks to the *ruach* as breath and calls it from the four *ruchot*, the four winds, that is, from every direction (42:20; Daniel 8:8). The wind becomes breath for the bodies. The play prepares for verse 14, where the LORD says the life he gives is his own Spirit. Jesus uses the same play on wind and Spirit in John 3:8.

decisions.choice: these slain: people killed in battle
decisions.reason: The word means those who have been killed. The bones are the remains of a slaughtered people, Israel destroyed by war and exile (verse 11).

decisions.choice: breath (L, B, R); winds (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level says "breath" for the *ruach* that is addressed and "winds" for the four directions (m1). Literal says "breathe on", Balanced and Readable "breathe into". The message takes no quotation marks of its own, as in verse 4.

decisions.choice: fôlego; ventos; sopra
decisions.reason: Ruach is addressed as breath and called from the four winds, the same Hebrew word in two senses (m1); Portuguese keeps "fôlego" for the breath, "ventos" for the four directions, and the verb "soprar", which belongs to both breath and wind, so that the play is felt. "Estes que foram mortos" says that they were killed, as the Hebrew word does (m2), where "estes mortos" would only say that they are dead.

en.R: So I prophesied as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told me to. Breath came into the bodies, and they came back to life. They stood up on their feet. There were so many of them that they were like a huge army.

decisions.choice: an army: a great host
decisions.reason: The word *chayil* means strength, and so an army. The dead have become a living host, a people again.

decisions.choice: they lived and stood on their feet: as Ezekiel himself was raised
decisions.reason: The Spirit set Ezekiel on his feet in 2:2 and 3:24. Now the people, too, are raised up. Revelation 11:11 uses the words of this verse for the two witnesses: "the breath of life from God entered into them, and they stood on their feet".

decisions.choice: breath (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: *Ruach* is "breath" here, as in verses 5-9. Readable adds "like" to make the picture plain.

pt.R: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Filho do homem, estes ossos são todo o povo de Israel. Eles dizem: 'Os nossos ossos estão secos. Não temos mais esperança. Estamos acabados.'

decisions.choice: these bones are the whole house of Israel: the vision explained
decisions.reason: The vision is not about individual people raised from the dead but about the nation, dead in exile, which the LORD will bring back to life and to its land (verses 12-14). "The whole house of Israel" includes both kingdoms (verses 15-22).

decisions.choice: our bones are dried up; we are cut off: the exiles' despair
decisions.reason: The people speak as if they were dead already, with no strength and no future (compare Psalm 31:11; Proverbs 17:22; Lamentations 3:54). The vision takes their own words and answers them.

decisions.choice: cut off completely (L); completely cut off (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "for ourselves", which stresses the verb. The people's words are quoted inside the LORD's words, so they take single quotation marks inside the double ones.

decisions.choice: I will open your graves: the return from exile pictured as resurrection
decisions.reason: The picture changes from bones in a valley to bodies in graves, but the meaning is the same: the LORD will bring his people back from the death of exile to their land. The passage does not set out a teaching about the resurrection of the body, but it shows the LORD as the one who can raise the dead, and later Scripture speaks of a bodily resurrection in similar words (Isaiah 26:19; Daniel 12:2; John 5:28-29).

decisions.choice: my people: the people the LORD still claims
decisions.reason: The LORD calls the despairing exiles "my people" (verse 13). His covenant with them is not over.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. The message takes no quotation marks of its own, as in verse 4. Readable starts a new sentence with "My people", where the pronoun is capitalized under either setting.

decisions.choice: my Spirit: the LORD's own Spirit, the source of the people's new life
decisions.reason: The *ruach* that was breath in verses 5-10 is now named as the LORD's own Spirit. The same promise is given in 36:27 and 39:29. The people's new life is not their own strength but God's Spirit in them.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD: the name alone
decisions.reason: The formula here has the divine name alone, not "the Lord GOD", as in a few other places in the book.

decisions.choice: Spirit, capitalized; I, the LORD, have spoken; declares (L, B) / says (R) the LORD
decisions.reason: Here *ruach* is the LORD's own Spirit, capitalized by Isaiah's rule as at 2:2. "I, the LORD, have spoken" and *ne'um* follow the settled wording. The closing quotation mark ends the LORD's words begun in verse 9.

decisions.choice: o meu Espírito; declara o SENHOR (L, B); diz o SENHOR (R)
decisions.reason: The ruach that was breath in verses 5-10 is now the LORD's own Spirit (m1), so Portuguese moves from "fôlego" to "Espírito", as the English moves from "breath" to "Spirit". Ne'um is "declara" at Literal and Balanced and "diz" at Readable, as Isaiah 1:24 and Jeremiah 1:8 set it in Portuguese.

decisions.reason: A new message, with a sign Ezekiel acts out (as in chapters 4-5 and 12): two sticks joined in his hand, showing that Israel and Judah will be one nation again.

decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. What follows is the LORD's message, which takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, take for yourself one stick and write on it, For Judah and for [the] sons of Israel his companions; and take one stick and write on it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all [the] house of Israel his companions.

pt.B: Quanto a ti, filho do homem, toma uma vara e escreve nela: "De Judá e dos israelitas aliados a ele." Depois toma outra vara e escreve nela: "De José, isto é, a vara de Efraim, e de toda a casa de Israel aliada a ele."
pt.R: Filho do homem, pega uma vara e escreve nela: "Esta pertence a Judá e ao povo de Israel que está unido a ele." Depois pega outra vara e escreve nela: "Esta pertence a José, isto é, a Efraim, e a todo o povo de Israel que está unido a ele."

decisions.choice: Judah and Joseph, the stick of Ephraim: the southern and the northern kingdoms
decisions.reason: After Solomon the people split into two kingdoms: Judah in the south, with Jerusalem, and Israel in the north, often called Ephraim after its largest tribe, which descended from Joseph (1 Kings 12). The northern kingdom was taken into exile by Assyria in 722 BC, and Judah by Babylon in 597-586 BC.

decisions.choice: a stick: a piece of wood
decisions.reason: The word *'ets* means wood, a stick or a staff. It may be a plain stick, or a wooden writing board. Numbers 17:16-26 tells of a staff for each tribe with its name written on it.

decisions.choice: his companions: the tribes joined to him
decisions.reason: Judah was joined by Benjamin and by people from other tribes who came south (2 Chronicles 11:12-17); Ephraim stood for the other northern tribes.

decisions.choice: stick (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level says "stick", the plainest word for the object (m2). The words written on the sticks take double quotation marks, as text quoted inside the LORD's message. Literal says "associated with him" for "his companions"; Readable says "joined to it".

decisions.choice: uma vara (every level)
decisions.reason: The word is a piece of wood, a stick or a staff (m2). "Vara" is the plain Portuguese word for a straight stick, and it is the word for the tribes' staffs of Numbers 17, which the meaning note recalls.

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L); os israelitas (B), with no gender setting
alternatives: os filhos e filhas de Israel
decisions.reason: As the Old Testament terms set it: "filhos" already includes daughters and "israelitas" names the whole people, so Portuguese needs no gender setting where the English has one; the same holds for "os filhos do teu povo" (verse 18) and "os seus filhos" (verse 25).

records.literal_gloss: Speak to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I am taking the stick of Joseph, which [is] in [the] hand of Ephraim, and [the] tribes of Israel his companions, and I will put them with it, [with] the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they will be one in my hand.

en.L: say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which [is] in Ephraim's hand, and the tribes of Israel, his associates, and I will set them upon it, [upon] the stick of Judah, and I will make them into one stick, and they will be one in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.
en.B: tell them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim's hand, and of the tribes of Israel associated with him, and join it to the stick of Judah. I will make them a single stick, and they will become one in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.
en.R: Then tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which Ephraim holds, and of the tribes of Israel joined to it. I will join it to the stick of Judah and make them one stick. They will be one in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand.

pt.L: dize a eles: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Eis que eu tomarei a vara de José, que [está] na mão de Efraim, e as tribos de Israel, os seus companheiros, e as porei sobre ela, [sobre] a vara de Judá, e farei deles uma só vara, e serão uma [só] na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão.
pt.B: dize a eles: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Vou tomar a vara de José, que está na mão de Efraim, e das tribos de Israel associadas a ele, e vou juntá-la à vara de Judá. Farei delas uma só vara, e elas serão uma só na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão.
pt.R: Então dize a eles: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Vou pegar a vara de José, que está nas mãos de Efraim, e das tribos de Israel unidas a ele. Vou juntá-la à vara de Judá e fazer delas uma só vara. Elas serão uma só na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão.

decisions.choice: one in my hand: the LORD makes the two peoples one
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel's hand the sticks are a sign; in the LORD's hand they become one in fact. The split of 1 Kings 12 will be healed.

decisions.choice: I will put them with it, with the stick of Judah: the Hebrew is awkward
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "I will put them on it, the stick of Judah". The sense is plain: the northern tribes will be joined to Judah.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Verse 19 begins with "Speak to them" and completes the sentence of verse 18, so it starts with a small letter at Literal and Balanced. The message takes no quotation marks of its own.

source.text: וְהָי֨וּ הָעֵצִ֜ים אֲֽשֶׁר־תִּכְתֹּ֧ב עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם בְּיָדְךָ֖ לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the sticks on which you write will be in your hand before their eyes,

en.L: And the sticks on which you write shall be in your hand before their eyes,
en.B: Hold the sticks you have written on in your hand where they can see them,
en.R: Hold the sticks you wrote on in your hand where the people can see them.

pt.L: E as varas em que escreveres estarão na tua mão diante dos olhos deles,
pt.B: Segura na mão as varas em que escreveste, à vista deles,
pt.R: Segura na mão as varas em que escreveste, de modo que o povo possa vê-las.

decisions.choice: in your hand before their eyes: the sign is shown as the words are spoken
decisions.reason: The sign is held up while Ezekiel speaks the words of verses 21-28.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on (L, B)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 21, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

source.text: וְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנִ֤י לֹקֵ֨חַ֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִבֵּ֥ין הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָֽלְכוּ־שָׁ֑ם וְקִבַּצְתִּ֤י אֹתָם֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אוֹתָ֖ם אֶל־אַדְמָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and speak to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I am taking [the] sons of Israel from among the nations where they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them to their land.

en.L: and say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am going to take the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from among the nations to which they have gone, and gather them from every side, and bring them to their own soil.
en.B: and say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am going to take the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from all around and bring them back to their own land.
en.R: Then tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to take the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from all around and bring them home to their own land.

pt.L: e dize a eles: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Eis que eu tomarei os filhos de Israel do meio das nações para onde foram, e os reunirei de todos os lados, e os trarei para o seu solo.
pt.B: e dize a eles: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Vou tirar os israelitas do meio das nações para onde foram. Vou reuni-los de todos os lados e trazê-los de volta para a sua própria terra.
pt.R: Depois dize a eles: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Vou tirar os israelitas do meio das nações para onde eles foram. Vou reunir esse povo de todos os lados e trazê-lo de volta para a sua própria terra.

decisions.choice: I will take, gather and bring them: as 36:24
decisions.reason: The promise repeats 11:17; 34:13 and 36:24, here for both kingdoms.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. "The sons of Israel" follows the settled wording: "children" (L) and "Israelites" (B, R) through the gender setting.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֣יתִי אֹ֠תָם לְג֨וֹי אֶחָ֤ד בָּאָ֨רֶץ֙ בְּהָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמֶ֧לֶךְ אֶחָ֛ד יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לְכֻלָּ֖ם לְמֶ֑לֶךְ וְלֹ֤א יִֽהְיוּ־עוֹד֙ לִשְׁנֵ֣י גוֹיִ֔ם וְלֹ֨א יֵחָ֥צוּ ע֛וֹד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י מַמְלָכ֖וֹת עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make them one nation in the land, on [the] mountains of Israel, and one king will be king for all of them; and they will no longer be two nations, and they will no longer be divided again into two kingdoms.

en.L: And I will make them into one nation in the land, on Israel's mountains, and one king will be king for all of them; and they will no longer be two nations, and no longer be divided into two kingdoms.
en.B: I will make them into a single nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, with one king ruling over them all. Never again will they be two nations or be split into two kingdoms.
en.R: In the land, on the mountains of Israel, I will make them one nation. They will all have one king. They will never again be two nations or be divided into two kingdoms.

pt.L: E farei deles uma [só] nação na terra, nos montes de Israel, e um [só] rei será rei para todos eles; e não serão mais duas nações, e não mais serão divididos em dois reinos.
pt.B: Farei deles uma só nação na terra, nos montes de Israel, e um único rei reinará sobre todos eles. Nunca mais serão duas nações nem estarão divididos em dois reinos.
pt.R: Na terra, nos montes de Israel, farei deles uma só nação. Todos eles terão um só rei. Nunca mais vão ser duas nações nem vão ficar divididos em dois reinos.

decisions.choice: one nation, one king: the end of the division
decisions.reason: The two kingdoms had been divided since about 930 BC, and the north had been in exile for well over a century. The LORD promises to make them one again under one king (Hosea 2:2; Jeremiah 3:18).

decisions.choice: king: *melekh*
decisions.reason: Here the coming ruler is called "king", the usual word; in verses 24-25 he is called king and prince (see 34:24).

decisions.choice: king (L, B); rule (R)
decisions.reason: The word *melekh* is "king" at every level; Readable says "one king will rule" for "one king will be king".

source.text: וְלֹ֧א יִֽטַמְּא֣וּ ע֗וֹד בְּגִלּֽוּלֵיהֶם֙ וּבְשִׁקּ֣וּצֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְכֹ֖ל פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֑ם וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּ֣י אֹתָ֗ם מִכֹּ֤ל מוֹשְׁבֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטְא֣וּ בָהֶ֔ם וְטִהַרְתִּ֤י אוֹתָם֙ וְהָיוּ־לִ֣י לְעָ֔ם וַאֲנִ֕י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will no longer defile themselves with their idols and with their detestable things and with all their transgressions; and I will save them from all their dwelling places in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them; and they will be my people, and I will be their God.

en.L: And they will no longer defile themselves with their filthy idols and their detestable things and all their transgressions; and I will save them from all their dwelling places in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them; and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.
en.B: They will no longer make themselves unclean with their idols, their vile idols or any of their rebellious acts. I will rescue them from all the places where they lived and sinned, and I will make them clean. They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.
en.R: They will no longer make themselves unclean by worshiping their idols and their disgusting idols or by any of their other sins. I will save them from all the places where they lived and sinned, and I will make them clean. They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

pt.L: E não se contaminarão mais com os seus ídolos imundos, e com as suas coisas detestáveis, e com todas as suas transgressões; e os salvarei de todos os lugares em que habitaram, nos quais pecaram, e os purificarei; e eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo, e eu serei o seu Deus.
pt.B: Não se tornarão mais impuros com os seus ídolos, com os seus ídolos vis, nem com nenhum dos seus atos de rebeldia. Eu os livrarei de todos os lugares onde moraram e pecaram, e os purificarei. Eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo, e eu serei o Deus deles.
pt.R: Eles não vão mais se tornar impuros adorando os seus ídolos e os seus ídolos repugnantes, nem com nenhum dos seus outros pecados. Vou salvá-los de todos os lugares onde moraram e pecaram, e vou purificá-los. Eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo, e eu serei o Deus deles.

decisions.choice: their dwelling places: possibly "their backslidings"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "all their dwelling places in which they sinned". With a small change in two letters, the word reads "their turnings away", that is, their unfaithfulness, and the Septuagint seems to read it so. The standard Hebrew text is kept: the LORD will save them from the places where they sinned.

decisions.choice: they will be my people, and I will be their God: the covenant formula
filthy idols, detestable things, transgressions (L); idols, vile idols, rebellious acts (B); idols, disgusting idols, sins (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *gillulim*, *shiqqutsim* and *pesha'* in Ezekiel.

decisions.choice: ídolos imundos, coisas detestáveis, transgressões (L); ídolos, ídolos vis, atos de rebeldia (B); ídolos, ídolos repugnantes, pecados (R)
decisions.reason: Gillulim and shiqqutsim in the wording 6:4 and 5:11 set for the book in Portuguese, level by level as the English: Literal "ídolos imundos" for Ezekiel's scornful word, Balanced and Readable "ídolos". The covenant formula has "o seu Deus" at Literal, as 11:20.

source.text: וְעַבְדִּ֤י דָוִד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְרוֹעֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד יִהְיֶ֣ה לְכֻלָּ֑ם וּבְמִשְׁפָּטַ֣י יֵלֵ֔כוּ וְחֻקֹּתַ֥י יִשְׁמְר֖וּ וְעָשׂ֥וּ אוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And my servant David [will be] king over them, and one shepherd will be for all of them; and in my judgments they will walk, and my statutes they will keep and do them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David [will be] king over them, and one shepherd there will be for all of them; and they will walk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and do them.
en.B: My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings and be careful to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes.
en.R: A king from the family of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will rule over them. All of them will have one shepherd. They will live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules and carefully obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws.

pt.L: E o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Davi [será] rei sobre eles, e um só pastor haverá para todos eles; e andarão nos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} juízos, e guardarão os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos e os cumprirão.
pt.B: O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Davi será rei sobre eles, e todos terão um só pastor. Seguirão as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} ordenanças e cuidarão de cumprir os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos.
pt.R: Um rei da família do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Davi vai reinar sobre eles. Todos eles terão um só pastor. Eles vão viver de acordo com as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} regras e obedecer com cuidado às {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} leis.

decisions.choice: my servant David, king, one shepherd: 34:23-24
decisions.reason: See 34:23. Here the coming David is called "king" (*melekh*) as well as shepherd; in verse 25 he is "prince". Under him the people will at last keep the LORD's law, as 36:27 promised.

decisions.choice: servant; judgments, statutes (L); rulings, statutes (B); rules, laws (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *'eved* (34:23) and for the LORD's commands in Ezekiel. Readable says "a king from the family of" as in 34:23. Balanced begins the sentence with "My", where the pronoun is capitalized under either setting.

decisions.choice: o meu servo Davi (every level); juízos, estatutos (L); ordenanças, estatutos (B); regras, leis (R)
decisions.reason: As 34:23: "servo" at every level for 'eved here, a title of honour for the king (m1), not the "escravo" the Old Testament terms give Literal for slavery. The LORD's commands follow the English levels, with "estatuto" and "ordenança" as the Old Testament terms.

source.text: וְיָשְׁב֣וּ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָתַ֨תִּי֙ לְעַבְדִּ֣י לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָֽשְׁבוּ־בָ֖הּ אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְיָשְׁב֣וּ עָלֶ֡יהָ הֵ֠מָּה וּבְנֵיהֶ֞ם וּבְנֵ֤י בְנֵיהֶם֙ עַד־עוֹלָ֔ם וְדָוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י נָשִׂ֥יא לָהֶ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will dwell on the land that I gave to my servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt; and they will dwell on it, they and their sons and their sons' sons forever; and David my servant [will be] prince for them forever.

en.L: And they will dwell in the land that I gave to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt; and they will dwell in it, they and their {{gender:children|sons}} and their {{gender:children's children|sons' sons}} forever; and David {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant [will be] their prince forever.
en.B: They will live in the land I gave to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, the land where your ancestors lived. They will live there forever, they and their children and their grandchildren, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will be their prince forever.
en.R: They will live in the land I gave to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, where your ancestors lived. They and their children and grandchildren will live there forever. And the king from the family of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David will be their ruler forever.

pt.L: E habitarão na terra que dei ao {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jacó, na qual habitaram os pais de vocês; e habitarão nela, eles e os seus filhos e os filhos dos seus filhos para sempre; e Davi, o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo, [será] o príncipe deles para sempre.
pt.B: Eles viverão na terra que dei ao {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jacó, a terra onde os antepassados de vocês viveram. Viverão ali para sempre, eles, os seus filhos e os seus netos, e o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Davi será o príncipe deles para sempre.
pt.R: Eles vão morar na terra que dei ao {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jacó, onde os antepassados de vocês moraram. Eles, os seus filhos e os seus netos vão morar ali para sempre. E o rei da família do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Davi será o governante deles para sempre.

decisions.choice: prince: see 34:24
decisions.reason: The ruler is called *nasi'*, "prince", as in 34:24 and chapters 44-48.

decisions.choice: forever: a lasting kingdom
decisions.reason: The promise recalls the LORD's promise to David that his throne would stand forever (2 Samuel 7:13-16; Psalm 89:4-5). Luke 1:32-33 speaks of Jesus' reign in these terms.

decisions.choice: servant (L, B, R); prince (L, B); ruler (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *'eved* and *nasi'*. "Children" and "children's children" take the gender setting at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "children and grandchildren".

decisions.choice: o príncipe (L, B); o governante (R)
decisions.reason: Nasi' as the English levels (m1), the word chapters 44-48 use for the ruler: "príncipe" at Literal and Balanced, "governante" at Readable.

source.text: וְכָרַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ בְּרִ֣ית שָׁל֔וֹם בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם יִהְיֶ֣ה אוֹתָ֑ם וּנְתַתִּים֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אוֹתָ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֧י אֶת־מִקְדָּשִׁ֛י בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make for them a covenant of peace; an everlasting covenant it will be with them; and I will give them and multiply them, and I will set my sanctuary in their midst forever.

en.L: And I will make for them a covenant of peace; a covenant of perpetuity it will be with them; and I will establish them and increase them, and I will place {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary in their midst forever.
en.B: I will make a covenant of peace with them, a covenant that will last forever. I will establish them and make them numerous, and I will place {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary among them forever.
en.R: I will make a peace agreement with them that will last forever. I will settle them in the land and make them grow in number. I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple among them forever.

pt.L: E farei com eles uma aliança de paz; uma aliança perpétua será com eles; e os estabelecerei e os multiplicarei, e porei o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} santuário no meio deles para sempre.
pt.B: Farei com eles uma aliança de paz, uma aliança que vai durar para sempre. Eu os estabelecerei e os farei numerosos, e porei o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} santuário no meio deles para sempre.
pt.R: Farei com eles um acordo de paz que vai durar para sempre. Vou firmá-los na terra e fazer com que sejam muitos. Vou pôr o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} templo no meio deles para sempre.

decisions.choice: a covenant of peace, an everlasting covenant: 34:25 and 16:60
decisions.reason: The covenant of peace of 34:25 is called "everlasting", as in 16:60 and Isaiah 55:3; 61:8.

decisions.choice: I will give them: the sense is uncertain
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "I will give them". It may mean "I will establish them" or "I will set them [in their land]". The Septuagint does not have these words.

decisions.choice: my sanctuary in their midst forever: the LORD's presence among his people
decisions.reason: The sanctuary that the glory left (10:18-19; 11:22-23) will be set among the people forever. Chapters 40-48 describe it.

decisions.choice: a peace agreement (R); temple (R)
decisions.reason: As at 34:25, Readable says "agreement" for "covenant", and "temple" for "sanctuary", as at 11:16.

source.text: וְהָיָ֤ה מִשְׁכָּנִי֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָיִ֥יתִי לָהֶ֖ם לֵֽאלֹהִ֑ים וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ־לִ֥י לְעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And my dwelling place will be over them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dwelling place will be with them; and I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.
en.B: My dwelling place will be among them, and I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.
en.R: I will live among them, and I will be their God, and they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

pt.L: E a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} morada estará com eles; e serei o seu Deus, e eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo.
pt.B: A {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} morada estará no meio deles; eu serei o Deus deles, e eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo.
pt.R: Vou morar no meio deles. Eu serei o Deus deles, e eles serão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo.

decisions.choice: my dwelling place will be with them: the LORD will live among them
decisions.reason: The word *mishkan* is the word used for the tabernacle, the tent where the LORD lived among Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 25:8-9). The preposition can mean "over" or "with"; the sense is that the LORD's presence will rest among and over his people.

decisions.choice: my dwelling place with them; I will be their God: 2 Corinthians 6:16 and Revelation 21:3
decisions.reason: Paul quotes these words, joined with Leviticus 26:11-12, to say that the church is the temple of the living God (2 Corinthians 6:16). Revelation 21:3 uses them of the new creation: "the dwelling of God is with human beings". John 1:14 says that the Word "tabernacled among us".

decisions.choice: dwelling place ... with them (L, B); I will live with them (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "with them" for the preposition, which fits both senses (m1). Readable says plainly what the dwelling place means. Balanced begins with "My", capitalized under either setting.

decisions.choice: a minha morada
decisions.reason: Mishkan is the tabernacle's word (m1), but here it is the LORD's dwelling among his people, and "morada" is the word Revelation 21:3 uses in Portuguese for the same promise (m2), so the link is kept.

records.literal_gloss: And the nations will know that I, Yahweh, sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary is in their midst forever.

en.L: And the nations will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, make Israel holy, when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary is in their midst forever.
en.B: Then the nations will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, make Israel holy, when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary is among them forever.
en.R: Then the nations will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have made Israel holy, because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple will be among them forever.

pt.L: E as nações saberão que eu, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, santifico Israel, quando o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} santuário estiver no meio deles para sempre.
pt.B: Então as nações saberão que eu, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, santifico Israel, quando o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} santuário estiver no meio deles para sempre.
pt.R: Então as nações saberão que eu, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, tornei Israel santo, porque o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} templo estará no meio deles para sempre.

decisions.choice: I, the LORD, sanctify Israel: Leviticus 20:8
decisions.reason: The words are those of the holiness laws: "I am the LORD who makes you holy" (Leviticus 20:8; 22:32). The LORD's presence among his people sets them apart as his.

decisions.choice: make holy (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb *qadash* means to make holy, to set apart. Each level says "make holy", so that the link with "sanctuary" (holy place) is kept in sense.

decisions.choice: santifico (L, B); tornei ... santo (R)
decisions.reason: "Santificar" keeps the link with "santuário" in the same sentence, as the English decision asks; Readable says "tornei santo", the plain words.
